full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J : This Criminal Petition for leave to appeal has been directed against the judgment and order dated 24-4-2011 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 11845 of 2011 summarily rejecting the application for bail of the accused-petitioner. 

 2. The facts necessary for disposal of this criminal petition, in short, are that this accused-petitioner was put on trial in Nari-o-Shishu Case No. 40 of 2002 of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Rajbari on the allegation that he murdered his wife on demand of dowry. The tribunal found the accused-petitioner guilty of the charge and convicted him under section 11(Ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 and sentenced him to death. The tribunal sent the case record to the High Court Division for confirmation of death sentence under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on the basis of which Death Reference No. 99 of 2003 was started. This accused-petitioner also filed a jail appeal being No. 583 of 2003 against that conviction and sentence. A Division bench of the High Court Division heard both the death reference and the jail appeal together and disposed of by a single judgment rejecting the death reference and allowing the appeal and sent back the case record to the lower court for holding trial afresh in the light of observations made in the judgment. The learned Judges of the High Court Division made observation to the effect that though it was proved that the victim was done to death while she was living at the house of her husband (the present accused-petitioner) who failed to explain the cause of her death, but there were not sufficient evidence to prove that she was murdered for dowry. The High Court Division also directed the trial judge to conclude the trial expeditiously and to keep the accused in custody till conclusion of the trial. 

 3. Since, the trial of the case could not be concluded within reasonable time after it was sent back for fresh trial under proper law the accused-petitioner prayed for bail before the High Court Division and by the impugned judgment and order the High Court Division rejected the said prayer making observation that since there was definite direction from the High Court Division that the accused shall remain in custody till conclusion of the trial, the court had no jurisdiction to entertain his prayer for bail. 

 6. However, we direct the trial court concerned to conclude the trial of the case against this accused-petitioner within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.
